instruction: Sort all the data in the spreadsheet by the "Quantity" column in descending order.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to sort data by Date Time ascending and create a line chart. Successfully sorted the data but repeatedly failed at chart creation, getting stuck in the Chart Type dialog with Column chart selected for many turns before finally selecting Line near the end but running out of turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can sort spreadsheet data by column, navigate menus, open Insert > Chart dialog, select data ranges
metadata.failure_analysis: Model successfully sorted data but failed to complete chart creation. Got stuck in Chart Type dialog, repeatedly defaulting to Column type. Eventually found Line type but exhausted the 50-turn limit.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests sorting by a different column (Quantity descending instead of Date Time ascending). Same sort capability but different target column and order direction.
metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting spreadsheet data by Quantity column (E) descending. Getter reads column E values and checks descending order. Metric gives 0.7 for correct sort, 0.15 for row count preservation, 0.15 for correct first quantity value (124).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads column E (Quantity) values from row 2 onwards and checks descending sort order
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('expected_row_count') and expected.get('expected_first_quantity')
Postconfig properly activates the window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation, ensuring fresh data is read
Scoring breakdown is reasonable: 0.70 for sort order, 0.15 for row count preservation, 0.15 for first value verification
All instruction requirements covered - the single requirement (sort by Quantity descending) is verified by checking sort order, data integrity, and correct max value at top
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter only verifies column E values are in descending order but does not verify that entire rows moved together (e.g., by spot-checking that the row with max Quantity still has its original associated data in other columns). This is a minor limitation since partial-column sorting is an unlikely failure mode in normal spreadsheet usage.
